rubric: Graded relevance per (candidate, job). Grade 2 = strong match: the job violates no hard constraint of the candidate AND the core occupation/skill fit is strong enough that a competent advisor would place it at the top of the list. Grade 1 = worth pursuing: no hard-constraint violation AND a credible partial or transferable-skill path exists; an advisor would include it with caveats. Grade 0 (implicit for every unlisted pair) = not worth the candidate's time; by definition this includes EVERY job that violates at least one hard constraint (location/commute, shifts, physical limitations, driving license, legally required certification, language level, citizenship/clearance, position percentage, disclosed salary below the candidate's floor, overnight travel). Labels were authored per-pair by reading the full candidate record against the full job record, BEFORE the first benchmark run, and are never edited to make any workflow look better; they change only to fix a demonstrable labeling error, documented in notes and in the commit message. Known bias: the labels were written by the same author as the matching logic and the taxonomy — see BENCHMARK.md 'Threats to validity'.
